claims.evidence: Witness photo shows a front sticker with “120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION” and a “2” icon, but no clearly readable brand/model or capacity number.
No low-voltage/voltage-rating text is readable in the provided observations.
Sticker label on the front shows “120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION”.
No evidence in the report of it being powered on, temperature tested, or compressor/operation observed.

risks.risk: Capacity may not be 250L (sticker text does not confirm the numeric capacity).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rating/capacity plate or label showing the exact liters (e.g., “250L”) and model/brand.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used chest freezer with unknown capacity (worst-case: smaller capacity).

risks.risk: Not actually working (compressor may be dead, thermostat faulty, or refrigerant leak).
risks.proof: A short video of it plugged in and running (compressor start sound/indicator), plus a temperature reading after a short period.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working / needs repair.

risks.risk: Cooling retention claim may be marketing only; lid seal/gasket may be weak causing poor retention.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the lid gasket/seal and a simple test: check for air gaps when closed; ideally a temperature-hold test clip.
risks.if_unproven: Price as poor retention due to possible seal issues.

risks.risk: Low-voltage operation may not be supported (may require stable power or have no inverter/voltage tolerance).
risks.proof: A photo of the electrical rating label showing voltage range (e.g., 110–240V or specific low-voltage tolerance).
risks.if_unproven: Price as standard-voltage equipment (worst-case: not suitable for low voltage).

risks.risk: Interior condition may be poor (heavy frost, leaks, bad cleanliness, missing baskets/trays).
risks.proof: Photos of the interior: frost level, cleanliness, drain area, and whether baskets/trays are included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as needing cleaning/defrost and possibly missing accessories.

risks.risk: Physical damage (dents, rust, hinge/latch issues) could affect sealing and longevity.
risks.proof: Full-body photos from multiple angles focusing on hinges, latch/handle, and any dents/rust.
risks.if_unproven: Price as cosmetically worn with potential sealing/hinge wear.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rating plate/label showing brand, model, exact capacity (liters), and voltage/wattage.
Video showing the freezer plugged in and running (compressor start and operation).
Interior photos: frost level, cleanliness, drain area, and whether baskets/trays are included.
Close-up photos of the lid gasket/seal and hinge/latch area.
Any evidence of maintenance/repair history (receipt or service note), if available.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a chest freezer and the “120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION” sticker, but key pricing drivers (exact capacity, working status, voltage tolerance, seal/interior condition) are not verifiable from the report. Proof is needed to avoid overpaying for a potentially non-working or mismatched unit.
